title: Five-year outcomes of trabeculo-canalectomy for Chinese PACG patients: a retrospective study

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License) - non-commercial, no derivatives, record kept private

indication: medically uncontrolled primary angle-closure glaucoma with peripheral anterior synechiae over more than 180 degrees, phakic eyes without obvious lens opacity, no previous eye surgery except laser iridotomy/iridoplasty (retrospective, single surgeon, Chinese patients; 50 eyes of 46 patients)

groups.description: trabeculo-canalectomy: half-thickness 4 x 4 mm scleral flap, removal of a 1 x 2 mm block of Schlemm's canal outer wall and trabecular meshwork, peripheral iridectomy, tight flap and conjunctival closure; no mitomycin C or 5-fluorouracil

series.notes: mean ± SD (table footnote); rows 1 wk, 1, 3, 6 mo, 1, 2, 5 y; per-visit N in Table 2 column C2 (all eyes through 1 y, fewer at 2 y and 5 y: ordinary attrition)

exclusions.what: Table 2 columns C4 (eyes with medications, count and %) and C5 (number of medication regimens)
exclusions.reason: counts and medication data are notes only

exclusions.what: Table 3 (total, absolute and qualified success, N (%))

exclusions.reason: graph of the same values as Table 2

exclusions.what: Methods visit list naming both '12 months' and '1 year'
exclusions.reason: Table 2 tabulates a single '1 y' row, which is used

notes: Role: the authors present trabeculo-canalectomy as their modification of trabeculectomy and as a novel bleb-independent procedure; this single cohort is therefore recorded as the treated (technique variant) arm. There is no comparison arm.

Context: recorded as trabeculectomy (a trabeculectomy variant without antimetabolite under a scleral flap, as framed by the authors and the triage note). The authors report no visible filtering bleb at 3 months in any eye; the protocol also allows 'other' for a novel procedure, so this context choice is an extraction ambiguity.
Analysis set: 20 eyes of 14 patients were excluded before analysis because follow-up was shorter than 3 months (selection by follow-up length, not by a postoperative outcome).
Reference kind: Table 2 reports all eyes on glaucoma medication preoperatively (inclusion: medically uncontrolled on two or more medications); no washout is described.
Method: the article does not name a tonometer.
Some patients contributed both eyes (50 eyes, 46 patients); means are over eyes.
Number of medication regimens (mean ± SD) and eyes with medications are tabulated per visit in Table 2 C4-C5 (not extracted).
Time conversions: 1 week = 0.23 months; years x 12.
